summary: Lynn Teskey Denton (1949–1995) was an Indology and religious studies scholar. She studied at McMaster University (BA, c. 1968–1972) and Somerville College (B.Litt., 1973–1975). She taught at McMaster (c. 1982–1995) and was Assistant Professor at Concordia University (1984–1989).

Lynn Thomas is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She earned her BA and MA at Lancaster University and completed her D.Phil at the University of Oxford by 1987. In 1997, she was a lecturer in Hinduism at the University of Roehampton.

László Gaál (1891–1964) worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology. He studied at Franz Joseph University (PhD c. 1913) and Göttingen under scholars including Andreas and Sieg. He held posts at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Debrecen.

Léon Feer (1830–1902) specialized in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology, studying under Foucaux, Pavie, Mohl, and Quatremère. He held posts at the INALCO, Collège de France, École Pratique des Hautes Études, and the Bibliothèque nationale de France.

Léon Rodet (1832–1895) was a scholar in the fields of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the École Polytechnique from circa 1851 to 1853 and was later a member of the Société Asiatique from circa 1878 to 1895.

Léon Vandermeersch (1928–2021) was a sinologist and philosopher educated at INALCO, the University of Paris, EPHE, and Paris Diderot University. His career included posts at the National Museum of Vietnamese History, Aix-Marseille, Paris Diderot, EPHE, Maison Franco-Japonaise, and EFEO.

Léonard Eugène Aurousseau (1888–1929) was a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. He studied at EPHE, INALCO, and under Édouard Chavannes. He spent his career at the École française d'Extrême-Orient, serving as a teacher and eventually as Director (1926–1929).

Lê Mạnh Thát (born 1944) works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He earned his BA at the University of Saigon (c. 1962–1965) and a PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (c. 1965–1974), later teaching at Vạn Hạnh University (c. 1974–1975).

M. A. Mehendale (1918–2020) was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He served as Joint Secretary of the Linguistic Society of India (attested 1955) and spent his career as a Sanskrit and Vedic literature professor at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute.

M. Athar Ali (1925–1998) was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He completed his studies at Aligarh Muslim University between circa 1948 and 1961, and worked there as a historian from circa 1953 to 1985.
M. Christopher Byrski (born 1937) is an Indology scholar who studied under Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz. He served as the Head of the Indology Department at the University of Warsaw, attested in 1991.

M. D. Balasubrahmanyam was an Indology and linguistics scholar who completed his dissertation at Savitribai Phule Pune University, where he also held a post. He later served as Reader at Ganganatha Jha Kendriya Sanskrit Vidyapeetha and Principal at Rashtriya Sanskrit Sansthan.

M. H. Krishna (1892–1947) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at Maharaja's College, Mysore, University of Madras, and UCL under Ernest Arthur Gardner and others. He was a professor, department head, and arts dean at the University of Mysore.

M. M. McCabe (born 1948) is a philosopher who studied at Newnham College and the University of Cambridge. She held posts at Newnham College, Murray Edwards College, King's College London (Professor 1990–2014), and University College London (c. 2014).

M. R. Raghava Varier (born 1936) is an Indology, linguistics, and history/archaeology scholar. Educated at the University of Calicut, the Archaeological Survey of India, and Jawaharlal Nehru University, he served as a professor at the University of Calicut from c. 1978 to 1996.

M. S. A. Rao (1926–1985) was an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Delhi and the University of Mumbai under Govind Sadashiv Ghurye. He held posts at the University of Delhi (c. 1959–1985), Syracuse University, and the University of Pennsylvania.

M. S. Nagaraja Rao (1932–2011) was an Indology and archaeology scholar educated at Mysore and Pune under M. N. Deshpande. He held posts at Karnatak University, the Karnataka State Archaeology Department, and served as Director General of the Archaeological Survey of India.

M. Seshagiri Sastri was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He served as Professor of Sanskrit at Presidency College, Chennai, Curator at the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library, and Professor of Sanskrit and Comparative Philology at Presidency University.
M. Shinoda (born 1977) is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Seiren Matsunami. He was educated at Agoura High School (circa 1991–1995) and the Art Center College of Design.

M. Victor Stanley (born 1866) worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Lawrence University, the University of Wisconsin-Madison (BA), the University of Oregon (MA), and Yale University (PhD), later serving as Supervising-Principal for the Corona-Norco Unified School District.
